messages:
jessica: customer escalated — updating address via /v1/accounts.update_address ended up invoking the billing-address update flow, not shipping. they noticed tax/charge recalculation and an invoice generated immediately :grimacing:
marc: ugh. do we have a repro payload?
jessica: pasted below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "account_id": "acct_foo",
  "address": {
    "line1": "123 Example St",
    "city": "Denver",
    "postal_code": "80202",
    "country": "US"
  }
}
```
jessica: note there is no explicit "address_type" or "target" field — previously router keyed off keys in payload and picked the first tool that accepted an "address" object
linh: that matches an autorouter heuristic we've seen — tools with overlapping signatures (both accept address object) get fuzzy-matched. the model picked update_billing_address_tool because its schema had a looser validation and higher prior probability
marc: does the runtime log show which tool id was chosen?
support-bot: tool-dispatch: chosen_tool=update_billing_address_tool, confidence=0.62, resolver=autorouter-v3, request_id=req_2026abc
jessica: customer impact: order had shipping scheduled still but billing change triggered billing workflow, they were charged tax difference. asked for immediate rollback + audit log
linh: quick repro steps I ran: 1) POST /v1/accounts.update_address with payload above 2) observe dispatch log 3) observe invoice.create invoked. i can share full logs in #eng-platform if needed
marc: can we short-term hotfix by adding a discriminator in the SDK (address_target = "shipping")?
linh: yes, but many clients call our generic endpoint. long-term: autorouter needs a stronger disambiguation rule — prefer explicit path param or require "address_type" when both tools are compatible
jessica: customer asked for a rollback and for us to prevent re-trigger. I put the invoice on hold and refunded the tax delta manually.
marc: action items: @eng-platform-oncall — patch autorouter fallback so when two tools share identical top-level keys we consult a small deterministic tie-breaker (tool priority metadata or explicit discriminator) rather than model score alone. also add metric to detect ambiguous dispatches > 0.5 confidence but with multiple matching signatures.
eng-platform-oncall: ack. i'll create an incident patch branch and add a safe server-side rule to prefer explicit "shipping" target when present, plus telemetry. will follow up with PR link.
jessica: leaving the customer handoff note in the ticket: refunded tax delta, put invoice on hold, engineering investigating autorouter change.
marc: thanks. possible follow-up: SDK patch to emit "address_target" and a doc note about ambiguous payloads. :+1:
